summary: All three conclusions follow from the stated hypotheses and accepted predecessor facts. The simplex-core argument handles every barycentric representation; the one-factor construction correctly converts positive interpolation weights into admissible metronoid masses, transfers intrinsic halfspace balance through the injective affine embedding, and supplies a common affine selector for the complete core; and the proper-rank estimate follows by injectively summing the pointwise fiber-volume bounds inside the saturated primitive slice. Zero weights, lower-dimensional fibers, whole-space pullbacks, nonsaturated embeddings, and the cases q<n and q=n are handled without a gap.
